column.text: Bitcoin surged past the critical psychological barrier of 70,000 today as a decisive bullish bias took hold across all major timeframes. The market closed with shorts being aggressively liquidated at a staggering rate of $401 million compared to mere $9.4 million in long positions, while spot ETF inflows added another +$189 million to the fuel tank. This aggressive momentum pushed Bitcoin up 5.6% on the day, driven by falling yields and ample stablecoin dry powder available for deployment into risk assets. However, traders must remain vigilant regarding extreme overbought conditions flashing across hourly charts for major names like ETH and SOL. The daily RSI sits at a concerning 71 with an hourly spike to 92, signaling aggressive momentum that often precedes a necessary pause rather than an immediate trend reversal given the expanding open interest of +8.74%. While dollar liquidity is contracting against these risk assets, creating macro headwinds for continuation longs, the fundamental strength remains undeniable. Retail investor activity has finally rebounded significantly after years of dormancy, suggesting Q3 marks the true bottom of this cycle according to recent data from Ansem. Meanwhile, regulatory clarity looms closer with the SEC proposing new crypto asset regulations and a White House summit scheduled for tomorrow. Despite these potential catalysts, the primary risk remains mean reversion before the next leg up can materialize.
